title: Number of Arithmetic Triplets
summary: Given a strictly increasing integer array nums and a positive integer diff, count the number of unique triplets (i, j, k) such that i < j < k, nums[j] - nums[i] equals diff, and nums[k] - nums[j] equals diff.
statement: Given a strictly increasing integer array nums and a positive integer diff, count the number of unique triplets (i, j, k) such that i < j < k, nums[j] - nums[i] equals diff, and nums[k] - nums[j] equals diff.
constraints: nums is strictly increasing and diff is positive.
Count index triples i<j<k with consecutive value differences both equal to diff.
Each starting value identifies at most one valid triple.
hints: Put all values in a set for constant-time membership checks.
Treat each array value as a possible first member.
Count it when value+diff and value+2*diff are both present.
Strict ordering makes those later values occur at later indexes and makes each valid triple’s start unique.
editorial: Strict ordering makes those later values occur at later indexes and makes each valid triple’s start unique.

tests.explanation: The triples with values 1,4,7 and 4,7,10 are valid.
Starting at four and five yields the two valid triples.
